before_summary:
- Approved E-Comm 911 police dispatch agreement; directed staff to report back on governance and finance (E-Comm).
- Adopted Community Standards Bylaw strengthening noise, nuisance and construction rules, with fines and enforcement (Bylaw 2255).
- Adopted rezoning to allow two‑lot subdivision at 897 Walfred Road; amenity payments required (Bylaw 2235).
- Gave first, second and third readings to rezoning for 3084–3096 Jacklin Road; maximize bicycle parking (Bylaw 2278).
- Issued a 36‑month temporary use permit for a cannabis retail store at 101‑977 Langford Parkway (TUP26-0003).
after_summary: The May 19, 2026 Regular Council meeting adopted multiple new policies and bylaws and approved several development and operational decisions: Adopted the Good Neighbour Policy (POL-0186-ADMIN) to clarify construction/contractor expectations. Approved multiple bylaws and readings including updated off-street parking (Bylaw 2272), several zoning amendments (including Jacklin Road rezoning and 2609 Sooke Road readings), and building energy/zero-carbon step code changes (Bylaw 2283). Issued Temporary Use Permit TUP26-0003 to Flight Cannabis Co. for 101‑977 Langford Parkway (36-month term). Directed staff to withhold 939 Klahanie rezoning from committee until unpermitted construction is brought into compliance. Authorized an extension/agreement with E-Comm 911 for dispatch services and requested a future report after governance reforms (Langford’s 2026 share approx. $2M).

before_summary:
- Gave first, second and third reading to 2026 Financial Plan and 2026 tax rates (Bylaws 2281 & 2282).
- Gave 1st, 2nd and 3rd readings to off‑street parking, removing City Centre minimums (Bylaw 2272); Wagner opposed.
- Consider bringing Bylaw 2278 forward for 1st–3rd readings to rezone 3084–3096 Jacklin Rd with affordability covenants.
- Directed staff to draft Zero Carbon Step Code bylaw: EL‑2 at 1 month, EL‑4 at 6 months.
after_summary: The council approved multiple land-use referrals and advanced climate, parking and community standards bylaws while adopting the Financial Plan readings. Directed staff to draft a Building Bylaw amendment to implement Zero Carbon Step Code (EL2 in 1 month; EL4 in 6 months for Part 9; Part 3 EL4 in six months) with in‑stream protection for existing projects. Approved notices / directions to proceed on several planning files: TUP26-0003 (Flight Cannabis), rezoning for 2609 Sooke Road and 3084/3088/3094-3096 Jacklin Road (with affordable housing/amenity contributions and covenants). Issued TUP26-0001 for Pawsitive Pet Emporium at 2899 Sooke Lake Rd and advanced multiple parking and community standards bylaws for readings/amendment. Gave first/second/third readings to park dedication and several regulatory bylaws and gave first/second/third readings to the 2026–2030 Financial Plan and Tax Rates bylaws (to come back for adoption).

before_summary:
- Approved the 2026‑2030 Financial Plan, setting a 10.47% 2026 tax increase; directed staff to prepare bylaws.
- Gave all three readings to Park Dedication Bylaw, dedicating 90 parcels (≈209 acres) as parks (Bylaw 2237).
- Directed staff to enter grant agreement with Habitat for Humanity per Attainable Home Ownership; bring housing bylaw.
- Authorized funding for four additional RCMP officers; direct staff to hire two now, hold funding for two.
- Gave first, second and third reading to Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255; rescinded noise permit and graffiti policies.
after_summary: Council received a BC Transit update and approved multiple land-use, bylaw and finance measures. Approved a grant agreement pathway with Habitat for Humanity and directed staff to prepare a housing agreement bylaw to secure long-term affordability. Adopted the 2026–2030 Financial Plan with amendments: authorized funding for four additional RCMP officers (two to be hired immediately; two held in abeyance pending working-group recommendations) and reallocated $155,000 in the capital budget to fix Bear Mountain Parkway temporary power. Gave three readings to the City of Langford Park Dedication Bylaw No. 2237 and first–third readings to Road Closure Bylaw No. 2246 (portion of Aldwynd Road) to expand Veterans Memorial Park. Gave 1st–3rd readings to Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255 and Amending Bylaw No. 2262 (including fines increase and permit transparency requirements).

before_summary:
- Received presentation of draft economic development strategy to guide growth, jobs, housing options, downtown vibrancy (EDCD Consulting).
- Confirmed staff will post slides, engagement report and a public survey on Let's Chat Langford (follow-up).
- Noted next steps: additional public engagement phases will follow before finalizing the strategy.
after_summary: The draft Economic Development Strategy was presented by EDCD Consulting and City staff and will be posted for public feedback with a follow-up survey. Council received the draft Economic Development Strategy (10 objectives) and noted priority actions including adding economic development staff capacity, creating a commercial/industrial land inventory, and launching a West Shore roundtable. Strategy priorities include business retention/expansion, investment readiness (including defence/marine supply chain positioning), downtown revitalization, and community wealth building. Councillors raised concerns about rising retail lease costs affecting small businesses, the need for childcare and public washrooms, and support for newcomers; staff confirmed these topics are addressed in the draft. Council approved the agenda as presented and subsequently adjourned at 6:55 pm.

before_summary:
- Adopted the City’s 2026–2030 financial plan, setting budgets and capital projects for 2026–2030 (Bylaw 2281).
- Adopted the 2026 property tax rates, fixing municipal tax rates by class for 2026 (Bylaw 2282).
- Approved the 2025 audited consolidated financial statements, finalizing last year's official city financial results (2025 Audited Statements).
after_summary: Council approved the 2025 audited consolidated financial statements and adopted the City’s 2026–2030 Financial Plan and 2026 Tax Rates bylaws. Approved the 2025 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. Adopted Bylaw No. 2281 (2026–2030 Financial Plan) and Bylaw No. 2282 (2026 Tax Rates). Heard a public submission expressing concern about the financial plan. Moved to close the meeting in-camera under s.90(1)(e) to consider acquisition/disposition of land. Meeting was adjourned at 7:51 p.m.

before_summary:
- Directed staff to recommend giving first, second and third readings of Langford Station bylaw (Bylaw 2265).
- Directed staff to recommend readings 1–3 for Animal Responsibility bylaw; feeding ban adds deer (Foxall opposed).
- Directed staff to opt out of public notification for The Loghouse Pub patio at 2323 Millstream Road.
- Directed staff to receive the 2025 West Shore RCMP annual report for information (West Shore RCMP).
after_summary: The Community Advisory Committee received the West Shore RCMP annual report and made recommendations on four reports: liquor licensing notification, Langford Station bylaw, and updated animal control bylaws (including an amendment to explicitly include deer). Received the 2025 West Shore RCMP Annual Report for information and engaged on priorities (property crime, mental health response, traffic enforcement, cybercrime). Recommended Council opt out of municipal public notification for The Loghouse Pub patio extension at 2323 Millstream Road. Recommended Council consider giving first, second and third readings to The Langford Station Bylaw No. 2265, 2026. Recommended Council give readings to Animal Responsibility Bylaw No. 2239 and Animal Control Amending Bylaw No. 2212 (amendment adopted to prohibit feeding 'dangerous wildlife or deer'); one committee member recorded opposition.

before_summary:
- Received Proposed 2026–2030 Five‑Year Financial Plan; staff presented proposed 15.13% 2026 tax increase (Feb 10 report).
- Received reduction options for the 2026 tax increase; impacts shown for 11%, 9%, 6%, 3% (Feb 19 report).
- Deferred budget decisions; Committee will consider budget survey results and deliberate March 17 (staff timeline).
- Heard public opposition to cuts affecting maintenance, safety, and the city website; speakers urged no deferment (public participation).
after_summary: Committee of the Whole received public input on the Proposed 2026–2030 Financial Plan and discussed reduction options for the 2026 tax increase. Members of the public urged Council not to cut maintenance or safety-related budgets and to avoid deferring necessary repairs. Staff confirmed the proposed 2026 tax increase (reported previously as ~15.13%) and identified funding sources including property taxes, prior-year surplus ($1.73M), grant funding ($1.55M), amenity/DCC and other reserves. Staff will report budget-survey results to Committee on March 17 and continue public participation at upcoming meetings in April. Staff clarified many capital projects are funded by DCCs, amenity/casino funds, grants or reserves (not immediate property-tax dollars); non-property revenues (e.g., building permits, licence-to-occupy) were discussed as limited options to reduce tax reliance.

before_summary:
- Directed staff to engage a consultant to verify and scope a municipally‑contracted residential curbside garbage service (waste report)
- Directed staff to increase public waste receptacle pickups from seven to fourteen weekly; no seasonal restrictions (waste)
- Directed staff to update off‑street parking and bicycle rules using options 1a and 4a; require five‑year review (Watt)
- Adopted housing agreements requiring affordable rental units at 2772 Vantilburg Crescent and 814 Hockley Avenue (Bylaws 2257, 2264)
- Approved a three‑year temporary use permit and development variance permit for a bakery at 116‑832 McCallum Road (TUP25‑0003/DVP25‑0003)
after_summary: Council received a one-hour presentation from Watt Consulting and directed staff to prepare an updated off-street parking bylaw (including removing minimums in the city centre) and create a 5-year review policy. Issued four Temporary Use Permits / Development Variance Permits for 116‑832 McCallum Rd (bakery), #101‑945 Reunion Ave (cannabis retail), 933 Tayberry Terrace (home business), and approved DVP for 932 Rowils Crescent. Adopted multiple bylaws including Housing Agreements (2772 Vantilburg Crescent; 814 Hockley Ave) and Park Dedication amendment; adopted City Centre Park Fees & Charges amendment. Directed increased public waste-receptacle service and to engage a consultant to verify a municipally‑contracted curbside garbage option, plus new receptacle standards. Approved municipal consent for CRD bylaws for West Shore RCMP expansion and added a policy to review off-street parking requirements every five years.

before_summary:
- Approved new purchasing rules letting CAO authorize purchases up to $75,000 goods/$200,000 construction; rescinded old policies (POL-0185-FIN).
- Approved Good Neighbour Policy requiring builders to sign acknowledgment and follow construction rules; Foxall opposed (POL-0186-ADMIN).
- Directed staff to ask Council to give first, second, third readings to Statutory Officers bylaw (Bylaw 2260).
after_summary: The Committee received a presentation from WorkLink BC on the START youth employment program and encouraged outreach to schools and employers. Adopted the Good Neighbour Policy (POL-0186-ADMIN) as presented; Committee Member Foxall opposed. Approved an updated Purchasing Policy (POL-0185-FIN) with multiple amendments (added training requirement for delegated purchasers, clarified CAO/Financial Officer exemption thresholds, added documentation and reporting requirements). Recommended that Council give first, second and third readings to the Statutory Officers & Delegation of Authority Bylaw No. 2260, 2026. Adopted the March 31, 2026 minutes and adjourned at 8:34 PM.

before_summary:
- Directed staff to prepare a report on Affordable Housing Reserve Fund history and past grants.
- Approved increasing construction-noise penalty to $1,000 (replaces $700, Bylaw 2262).
- Recommended Council give first, second and third reading to Park Dedication Bylaw No. 2237 (dedicates 90 lots).
- Recommended Council give first, second and third reading to Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255 (includes Bylaw 2262).
- Approved requiring noise permits be posted online before activities and strengthened subcontractor accountability (Bylaw 2255).
after_summary: The Community Advisory Committee met March 31, 2026 and made recommendations for Council on housing, bylaws, liquor referrals and park dedications. Recommended staff prepare a report summarizing the history and expenditures of the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund after a Habitat for Humanity presentation requesting per-door funding for up to 16 units. Recommended Council be advised that the City will opt out of provincial public notification for the Ryes & Shine Craft Distillery hours-change application at 103-2323 Millstream Road. Recommended Council give readings to Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255 (with amendments) and Misc. Amending Bylaw No. 2262 (including raising the construction-noise fine), and rescind two legacy policies. Recommended Council give readings to City of Langford Park Dedication Bylaw No. 2237 to formally dedicate ~209 acres of parkland.

before_summary:
- Directed staff to amend Election Bylaw to allow mail ballots; increased election budget by $15,000 (Bylaw 1819).
- Received the RCMP staffing request and community safety survey update for information (RCMP report).
- Approved consent to the CRD adopting Bylaw 4719 to dissolve the Traffic Safety Commission (Bylaw 4719).
- Rejected directing staff to write a letter joining the Judicial Review Coalition; Wagner and Mayor Goodmanson supported.
after_summary: Special Council received the community safety survey and advanced several operational items: Received the RCMP staffing request and Community Safety Survey; Council agreed to proceed with the report and discuss operational responses (superintendent requested 4 officers; consultant recommended funding 2 and holding a third in reserve). Directed staff to notify the public that Council will consider issuing a 3-year Temporary Use Permit for pet grooming at 2899 Sooke Lake Rd (motion carried). Consented to CRD Bylaw No. 4719 (Traffic Safety Commission amendments) and noted the CRD will assume the commission's assets/obligations. Authorized amendments to the Election Bylaw to allow mail ballots and added $15,000 to the election budget for implementation. Submitted notices of motion to study including a CRD director preference on the 2026 ballot and to ask the province to reopen Active Transportation grant funding and support safe routes to school (the latter motion carried).

before_summary:
- Approved recommending Council adopt the 2026–2030 five‑year financial plan, incorporating this meeting's budget changes (Financial Plan).
- Directed staff to reduce internal capital payment by $800,000; Guiry, Harder and Szpak opposed (Budget).
- Directed staff to cancel the city's Urban Development Institute membership and remove its fee budget; Goodmanson opposed (Budget).
- Directed staff to increase First Nation relations funding to $100,000, adding $50,000 from surplus (Budget).
- Directed staff to investigate alternate reserve funding for the Bear Mountain Parkway temporary power issue (Bear Mountain Parkway).
after_summary: Committee of the Whole completed budget deliberations on the proposed 2026–2030 Five‑Year Financial Plan and returned recommendations to Council. Reduced the Council Travel & Training budget by $30,000 and directed multiple line-item reductions (utilities, holiday decorations, etc.). Approved an $800,000 reduction to the internal capital payment for 2026 and directed staff to adjust future years accordingly. Directed staff to add $44,400 in funding (one-time) toward a Municipal Leaders Advisory Team Coordinator position for 2026. Increased the First Nations relations budget to $100,000 (additional $50,000 funded from surplus). Recommended Council approve the Proposed 2026–2030 Financial Plan as amended by Committee resolutions.

before_summary:
- Directed staff to prepare governance bylaw and remediation plan to address ~$19.6M internal debt (Breakdown of Internal Debt).
- Recommended transferring $850,000 from Capital Works Reserve to cover debt servicing; Guiry, Szpak, Wagner opposed (Budget).
- Directed staff to reduce City Hall staffing budget by $382,193; revisit 2024 organizational review recommendations (2026 Budget).
- Recommended removing the e-bike rebate program from the 2026 budget (2026 Budget Reports).
- Deferred the West Shore RCMP business case to a future Committee or Council meeting (West Shore RCMP).
after_summary: Committee received the public budget input and a detailed internal-debt breakdown and directed staff to create governance and remediation plans; it approved a package of 2026 budget reductions and deferrals to lower the proposed tax increase. Key actions: Directed staff to prepare a standing internal-borrowing governance bylaw and a remediation plan for all internal debt balances. Approved reductions and deferrals including a $382,193 reduction to City Hall staffing, removal of the e-bike program, deferral of the Garbage Can Retrofit to 2027, and a Royal Roads grant reduction (≈$65k). Approved transferring $850,000 from Capital Works Reserve to cover 2026 debt servicing and directed an increase of $300,000 in non-property revenues; cut travel/training by $120,000. Deferred the West Shore RCMP business case and set follow-up reporting timetables.

before_summary:
- Adopted Revenue Anticipation Borrowing Bylaw No. 2277, 2026 authorizing borrowing up to $20,000,000 (Bylaw 2277).
- Directed staff to write Premier and ministers requesting pause on Langford's Housing Target Order until funds reinstated.
- Directed staff to pay Tri-Way Neighbourhood Association ~$28,000 reimbursement for legal fees from Council contingency (Tri-Way).
- Resolved to amend the Manufactured Home Park Redevelopment Policy by deleting section 1(j) referencing the reserve fund.
- Adopted Sewer Utility Bylaw No. 2276, 2026 (Bylaw 2276).
after_summary: Council adopted updates to traffic, animal control, sewer and Langford Station bylaws, approved multiple temporary use permit directions, and advanced housing and election actions. Adopted four bylaws: Streets & Traffic amendments, Animal Responsibility & amendments, Langford Station bylaw and Sewer Utility amendment. Directed staff to notify issuance of a 3‑year Temporary Use Permit consideration for a home‑business at 116‑1064 Gala Court; refused the TUP request for 1041 Springboard Place. Received the interim Housing Target Progress Report (Sep 1, 2025–Feb 28, 2026) and directed staff to post and lobby the Province to pause Langford's Housing Target Order until provincial housing funds are reinstated. Approved reimbursement to the Tri‑Way Neighbourhood Association for legal fees (to be paid from Council contingency) and removed section 1(j) from the Manufactured Home Park Redevelopment Policy. Appointed Chief and Deputy Chief Election Officers for the 2026 municipal election.

before_summary:
- Received options to lower the 2026 property tax increase to 11%, 9%, 6% or 3% (Finance report).
- Adopted the Committee of the Whole minutes from February 10, 2026 (Carried).
- Approved the meeting agenda as presented (Carried).
after_summary: The Committee received a staff report outlining options to reduce the proposed 2026 property tax increase (proposed 15.13%) to target levels of 11%, 9%, 6% or 3% and discussed the service and financial trade-offs. Received the report for information; staff presented the dollar scale of options (1% = $622,061 city-wide; ≈$26.41 per average household). Staff highlighted reserve pressure (Capital Works & General Amenity reserves declining) and major capital pressures including ERP replacement and childcare/capital projects supported by grants. Reduction buckets (11/9/6/3%) were shown with estimated required cuts ($2.57M; $3.81M; $5.68M; $7.5M) and examples of potential impacts (staffing deferrals, parks/tree maintenance, storm/drainage, arena repairs). Committee emphasized waiting for public input (budget survey open to March 4; public COTW March 17 for deliberation) before final decisions.

before_summary:
- Approved Parks and Trails Master Plan; guides park and trail expansion, amenities and equity citywide (Adopted)
- Approved remedial order to clear vacant buildings at 810 Arncote Ave; City may enter after 60 days (RAO)
- Directed staff to report on mail-in ballots for the 2026 election by April 7, 2026 (report)
- Approved lease renewal with Victoria Conservatory of Music at Aquatics Centre; execution authorized after required notice (lease)
after_summary: Council adopted a 10–20 year Parks and Trails Master Plan and approved several operational actions on nuisance properties, elections, and facility leasing. Adopted the City of Langford Parks and Trails Master Plan as presented. Declared 810 Arncote Avenue a nuisance and imposed a remedial action order; if not remedied within 60 days of service the City will enter and complete the work at the owner's expense. Directed staff to report back on the implications of adding mail‑in ballots for the 2026 election by April 7, 2026. Approved renewal of the Victoria Conservatory of Music lease and authorized execution once Community Charter notice is given. Adopted the Consent Agenda (including minutes from Feb 2 and Feb 9).

before_summary:
- Directed staff to enter property and complete works at owner's expense if deadline missed (2748 Peatt Road).
- Directed staff to impose remedial action order requiring granular backfill buttress by Feb 25, 2026 (Peatt Road).
- Directed staff to authorize WSP Canada employees to enter the property for inspection (2748 Peatt Road).
- Directed staff to shorten reconsideration period to noon Feb 19, 2026 for owner.
after_summary: Council declared 2748 Peatt Road and 2745 Scafe Road (the "Scene") a hazard and imposed a Remedial Action Order after WSP identified unsafe shoring. Imposed a Remedial Action Order requiring the shoring wall at 2748 Peatt Rd/2745 Scafe Rd to be buttressed with engineered granular backfill and related works; completion shortened to February 25, 2026. Directed staff to shorten the reconsideration period to noon February 19, 2026, and authorized WSP to access the property for inspection. Directed that if owner does not comply by Feb 25 the City may enter the property and complete work at the owner's expense; costs are recoverable and may be added to property taxes if unpaid. Council emphasized safety (restricting heavy vehicles) and confirmed fire/rescue can access from Peatt Road rather than the affected lane.

before_summary:
- Presented proposed 2026–2030 five‑year financial plan, proposing a 15.13% 2026 tax increase (proposed plan).
- Directed staff to include Council pay increase, pro‑rated in 2026 for new Council term (Nov 2, 2026).
- Provided public engagement schedule: budget survey Feb 11–Mar 4; public input Feb 23 and Mar 17 (Langford.ca).
after_summary: The Committee received the proposed 2026–2030 Five-Year Financial Plan (staff presented a 15.13% proposed 2026 tax increase and the drivers behind it). Staff presented the proposed 2026–2030 Financial Plan with a proposed 2026 tax increase of 15.13%, driven by RCMP costs, E-Comm, debt servicing (aquatic centre), Woodlands Park tenant supports and CPI-linked contracts. Staff also presented options to reduce the 2026 tax increase to 11%, 9%, 6% or 3% (required budget reductions: ~$2.57M, $3.81M, $5.61M, and $7.55M respectively). Committee directed staff to include the proposed increase to council remuneration in the five-year financial plan, prorated for 2026 beginning with the new Council term (Nov 2, 2026) — fiscal impact noted in presentation (~$112,000). Committee approved the agenda, adopted the minutes, and adjourned; members were reminded the detailed reduction-options report will be released later this week and the meeting continues Feb 19.

before_summary:
- Recommended Council direct staff to obtain comprehensive review of a potential regional transportation authority by Sept 11, 2023.
- Received Capital Regional District transportation governance report for information.
- Received Capital Regional District presentation on regional transportation governance; staff answered Council questions.
after_summary: Committee heard a detailed CRD presentation on regional transportation governance and the CRD workbook to inform municipal feedback. Committee received the report and unanimously directed City staff to obtain a legal, governance, funding and service-level review for Langford, aiming to report to the Sept 11 Committee of the Whole. Staff confirmed CRD's engagement timeline (workbook due Sept 29; CRD analysis to November); City staff will provide additional commentary and options at Sept 11 and Sept 25. Major themes: funding tools, municipal autonomy vs regional authority, data/timing concerns (2014 plan vs new O/D survey), and how BC Transit / DCCs interact with any new regional model. No financial commitment was made at this meeting.

Confirmed Braden Hutchins and Adriana Proton as Deputy Corporate Officers and appointed Adriana Proton as signing authority for Council-approved contracts. after_summary: Council held a special meeting and updated Corporate Officer appointments. Rescinded the appointment of Braden Hutchins as Corporate Officer and appointed Marie Watmough as Acting Director of Corporate Services / Corporate Officer. Directed staff to prepare rezoning bylaws for 592 Phelps Ave (four small‑lot single‑family lots), 2762/2768 Claude Rd (proposed 10‑storey ~117 units), and 2845/2847/2850 Bryn Maur Rd (with portion of 737 Goldstream Ave) for a six‑storey ~93‑unit development. after_summary: Council approved multiple rezoning and variance applications, adopted a zoning bylaw, and advanced a 160-unit non-profit housing project. Directed staff to prepare rezoning bylaws for 592 Phelps Ave (four small‑lot single‑family lots), 2762/2768 Claude Rd (proposed 10‑storey ~117 units), and 2845/2847/2850 Bryn Maur Rd (with portion of 737 Goldstream Ave) for a six‑storey ~93‑unit development. before_summary:
- Approved closing the meeting to the public to discuss labour, land acquisition and early service negotiations.
- Approved the meeting agenda as presented.
- Adjourned the meeting at 4:08 p.m.
after_summary: Council met in a Special session focused on closing the meeting to the public for confidential matters and routine procedural business. Approved the agenda as presented. Passed a resolution to move into in-camera session under s.90(1)(c), (e) and (k) of the Community Charter for labour relations, land matters and preliminary service negotiations. Adjourned the meeting at 4:08 p.m.

before_summary:
- Adopted permissive tax exemptions for listed charities and community groups for 2024–2027 (Adopted Bylaw 2147).
- Adopted rezoning for 798 Gwendolynn Drive to allow six houses and 12 townhomes; Morley opposed (Bylaw 2137).
- Adopted zoning change removing extra parking requirement for three-bedroom apartments; Mayor opposed (Adopted Bylaw 2135).
- Gave first reading to rezoning 957 Walfred Road to allow 17 townhomes, subject to conditions (Bylaw 1927).
- Deferred approval of the 2023–2027 Council Strategic Plan pending staff analysis of public feedback (Strategic Plan).
after_summary: The council deferred adoption of the draft 2023–2027 Strategic Plan to allow staff time to analyze public feedback, referred a variance application back to committee for more background, and advanced multiple land-use approvals and bylaw adoptions. Referred the 2181 Bear Mountain Parkway variance back to the Sustainable Development Advisory Committee for further alternatives and rationale. Approved first reading of the 957 Walfred rezoning (Bylaw No.1927) with density bonus contributions and specific covenant conditions; public hearing to follow. Renewed a Temporary Use Permit for employee parking at 988 McCallum Road for three years and endorsed strata titling for 3193/3195 Glen Lake Rd (subject to removing a third driveway). Adopted four zoning/tax bylaws (Nos. 2135, 2137, 2147, 2148); the Mayor formally recorded opposition to Bylaw No. 2135. Large public participation on the Strategic Plan: main issues were insufficient public consultation, renter concerns, housing/parking, and reconciliation commitments.

before_summary:
- Rejected increase to Grant in Aid budget from $85,000 to $100,000; Yacucha opposed (Grant in Aid).
- Denied $10,000 funding request to Habitat for Humanity for affordable housing (Grant in Aid).
- Approved grants to local non-profits, including Big Brothers Big Sisters $5,000 (Grant in Aid).
- Approved recommending Council fund Royal Canadian Legion $6,000 annually from Community Events budget (Grant in Aid).
after_summary: The Community Advisory Committee reviewed the 2025 Grant-in-Aid submissions and made recommendations to Council on allocations and denials. Rejected a motion to increase the 2025 Grant-in-Aid budget from $85,000 to $100,000 (motion defeated). Recommended that Council consider annual $6,000 funding for the Royal Canadian Legion from the Community Events budget (motion carried). Approved Grant-in-Aid allocations totaling $85,000 across multiple organizations (approved list totals $73,000 in the first block and $12,000 in a subsequent block). Denied several large requests (including several PAC applications and Habitat for Humanity) and recommended those be refused through the Grant-in-Aid process.

- Appointed Councillor Yacucha as alternate to the West Shore Parks and Recreation Society Board.
after_summary: Special Council convened, moved into a closed in‑camera session, and made three board/committee appointments before adjourning. Passed a motion to close the meeting to the public under Community Charter section 90 for personnel, land and solicitor‑client matters. Appointed Councillor C. Harder to the Sustainable Development Advisory Committee for the remainder of the term. Appointed Councillor K. Yacucha as the alternate member to the West Shore Parks and Recreation Society Board. Appointed Councillor M. Morley as the City's alternate representative to the CRD Regional Water Supply Commission.

Approved a Development Variance Permit to reduce the interior side yard setback at 1900 Bear Mountain Parkway from 2.4 m to 1.5 m. before_summary:

after_summary: The Special Council meeting approved the purchase of the Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre and several associated financial and administrative actions. before_summary:

after_summary: Council met on November 21, 2022 and approved several administrative, grant and bylaw actions. before_summary:

after_summary: The Committee received the presentation of the draft 2024–2028 Financial Plan (including the proposed YMCA acquisition) and heard extensive public input on tax impacts and budget priorities. Presentation of the draft 2024–2028 Financial Plan included the potential purchase of the YMCA; staff confirmed the five-year plan still includes that acquisition and noted the City is currently paying $1.9M to Westhills Land Corporation (lease). Adopted Bylaw No. 2247 (Servicing Officer Designation).

after_summary: The Committee of the Whole received a presentation on the proposed 2023–2027 Five Year Financial Plan and heard extensive public input. before_summary:

after_summary: Council adopted the City’s Climate Action Plan and approved two permissive tax exemption bylaws. Council gave first, second and third readings to Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw Amendment No. 28 and to Solid Waste Collection Bylaw No. 2299. The Solid Waste bylaw passed amid extensive public opposition and the Mayor voting against it; residents raised estimated household fees of roughly $200–$300 per year, asked for an assisted‑pickup option, and questioned the timing before the election. Speakers broadly supported the Climate Action Plan but urged continued public engagement on implementation costs and service delivery.

before_summary:
- Approved hiring one additional Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer at $225,000 annual cost.
- Approved $50,000 small-business security grants, added one bike-patrol officer, and up to $50,000 Salvation Army agreement.
- Directed staff to draft Community Safety Plan by Dec 31, 2026, and a spray paint/bear spray bylaw.
- Adopted the City’s Housing Strategy as presented.
- Gave 1st, 2nd and 3rd readings to rezone 3213 and 3217 Happy Valley Road to mixed‑use village.
after_summary: Council approved Community Safety Working Group expenditures and measures including hiring one additional RCMP officer at $225,000/year, adding one full‑time bike patrol officer, a $50,000 small business security grant administered by the West Shore Chamber, and up to $50,000 to the Salvation Army for a service space. Council directed staff to launch Fire/RCMP business safety visits, a block/neighbourhood watch campaign, CPTED requirements for new housing, construction-theft prevention, trauma‑informed training for bylaw and fire staff, exploration of joint CRD bylaw patrols, and to draft a bylaw requiring spray paint and bear spray to be locked up. A proposal to create a mural program using MRDT funds was defeated after debate. Council also adopted the Housing Strategy, approved multiple zoning and permissive tax exemption bylaws and housing agreements, and directed staff to bring back a draft Community Safety Plan by December 31, 2026.

before_summary:

after_summary: Council approved the Asset Management Plan and Long‑Term Financial Plan to set long‑term infrastructure funding priorities. Council adopted OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 2292 embedding five master plans and a Future Street Network despite public criticism about engagement and the Transportation Plan. Council paused the 953 Walfred rezoning until the applicant removes an interior lot‑line setback and the proposed seven‑unit townhouse variance and returns revised plans. Council agreed to advance the 2639/2645 Sooke Road rezoning to readings subject to extensive pre‑adoption conditions; two councillors dissented. Council also adopted new fire prevention bylaws, approved a housing agreement at 2615 Sooke Road, advanced other housing agreements, and issued a 36‑month Temporary Use Permit for a cannabis retail store with strict conditions.

after_summary: Council adopted the new Fire Prevention and Regulation Bylaw No. 1665 and its amending bylaw No. 2286. Temporary Use Permit TUP26-0005 was issued for RV receiving/prep/storage at 4373 West Shore Parkway with conditions (no razor wire, an on-site 10 lb dry chemical extinguisher, posted address, and maintained fire access lane), and TUP26-0006 was issued to Code Ninjas at 890 Goldstream Avenue for a non-transferable three-year term. Council adopted zoning bylaws for 854 Latoria Road (Bylaw 2110) and Jacklin Road (Bylaw 2278), gave full readings to the Massie Drive zoning amendment (Bylaw 2236) and first reading to the omnibus OCP amendment (Bylaw 2292). Council rescinded and re-gave third reading to the Parks Development Cost Charge Bylaw No. 2291, adopted Park Dedication Bylaw 2288 and Reserve Fund amendment 2294, approved Housing Agreement Bylaw 2296 (2615 Sooke Road), and directed staff to write to the Minister and MLA urging reinstatement of ARC Foundation funding for SOGI 123.

before_summary:
- Directed Council to give first, second and third reading to fire prevention bylaw; creates fines (Bylaw 1665).
- Directed Council to give first, second and third reading to amending bylaw updating fire rules (Bylaw 2286).
- Adopted the Special Community Advisory Committee minutes from July 7, 2026.
after_summary: The Committee recommended that Council give first, second and third readings to Fire Prevention and Regulation Bylaw No. 1665, 2026 and the related Miscellaneous Amending Bylaw No. 2286, 2026; the motion carried. The draft bylaw consolidates existing fire and open‑burning rules, introduces fines and provides for limited post‑incident cost recovery. A public speaker challenged the three‑year delay since the 2023 Fire Master Plan, questioned fairness of charging homeowners for post‑incident costs and pointed out a historical date discrepancy. Committee members sought timeline clarification and confirmation that the bylaw aligns Langford with the provincial Fire Safety Act.

before_summary:
- Approved permissive tax exemptions: one-year for three nonprofits; ten-year for M’akola Housing Society (550 Goldstream Ave).
- Gave first, second and third readings to Parks Development Cost Charge Bylaw, establishing park DCCs (Bylaw 2291).
- Gave second and third readings to rezone 602 Madrona Place to residential, creating three lots (Bylaws 2253/2254).
- Adopted Transportation Master Plan and Active Transportation Plan; Hoffman Avenue connection removed from future street network (plans).
- Adopted updated form-and-character design guidelines and adopted Tree Protection Bylaw (Bylaws 2268/2269).
after_summary: Council adopted the Transportation Master Plan and Active Transportation Plan but removed the proposed Hoffman Avenue road connection from the Future Street Network pending further analysis. Council adopted updated Form and Character Design Guidelines (Bylaw 2268) and the new Tree Protection Bylaw (No. 2269). Council gave second and third readings to OCP and zoning amendments for 602 Madrona Place to convert a business-park lot into three R2 residential lots, with $1,000 per new lot to the Affordable Housing Reserve, $6,000 per lot to the General Amenity Reserve, and required Section 219 covenants. Permissive tax exemptions were approved (one year for three properties; ten years for M’akola Housing) and staff were directed to amend the bylaw to continue the exemption for 1319 Westhills Drive. Council issued DVP26‑0005 for subdivision at 1320 Westhills with no‑build and geotechnical covenant conditions, rescinded a package of council policies, and directed staff to notify the public that Council will consider Temporary Use Permits for a children’s coding school at 890 Goldstream and RV receiving/storage at 4373 West Shore Parkway.
